title: Service-level observability circuit-breaker and noise-aware rate limiter
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Certain noisy services generate repeated transient SLO violations that cause burn-rate alerts to cascade and oncall fatigue. Current burn-rate alerts are too sensitive to high-cardinality, short-lived spikes caused by downstream flakiness and batching artifacts.

Goal: Implement a service-level circuit-breaker style policy in the observability platform that can dampen noisy signals before they trigger paging, combined with a noise-aware rate limiter that dynamically adjusts alert thresholds using trace-derived sampling hints. The feature should preserve detection of real degradations while dramatically reducing false positive pages for noisy endpoints.

Scope:
- New policy engine component that evaluates SLO signals with temporal hysteresis and service-level backoff.
- Integrate trace hook-derived 'noise score' (from span rate, tail-latency bursts, and error burstiness) into alert scoring.
- Add a lightweight in-platform rate limiter that gates pages for services under a temporary circuit state.
- Dashboard and synthetic tests to validate reduced page volume and preserved detection fidelity.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term machine-learning anomaly models, major UI redesign of Console; follow-up will track ML model exploration.
acceptance_criteria: Circuit-breaker policy can be configured per-service and activates after configurable consecutive burn windows (default 3).
While circuit is open, paging is suppressed but alerts are still recorded and visible in a new 'quiet' state on the SLO dashboard.
Trace-derived noise score is computed at ingestion (<= 30s) and used to downweight burn-rate contributions from noisy spans.
Integration tests that replay historical incidents show >=50% reduction in pages for top-10 noisy services with <10% loss in true-positive alert rate.
Documentation exists in Confluence with configuration examples and runbook guidance; internal devs can enable/disable per environment via feature flag.
tasks: Design policy schema and config fields (service selector, consecutive windows, hysteresis, cooldown).
Implement policy engine with in-memory state and durable backing (KVS).
Add trace ingestion hook to compute per-service noise_score and annotate SLO events.
Wire noise-weighted burn calculation into existing burn-rate evaluator.
Expose circuit state in SLO dashboard and provide an opt-in page suppression toggle.
Create synthetic replay test harness and benchmark scripts.
Open PRs: platform (policy engine), ingestion (trace hook), frontend (dashboard tile).
Draft runbook and update oncall escalation docs.
notes: Tradeoffs: suppressing pages reduces immediate visibility — to mitigate we keep all suppressed events logged and surface a dedicated 'quiet' timeline so engineers can still inspect.
Decision: use a simple exponential backoff cooldown rather than fixed timer to adapt to repeated noise without complex ML for now.
Implementation detail: noise_score uses three signals: span_rate (spans/min), 95th latency burst ratio, and error-burst density across rolling 1m windows; normalized to [0,1].
Durability: use existing kv-store (config-store) for policy persistence; state is rebuildable from recent events on restart.
Rollout plan: feature-flag gated in staging, enable for internal non-prod services first, then opt-in for customers.
